components.note: 京 (jīng, high mound, capital) is a loose sound clue for jiù; going up to a high place fits 就 "to approach, to go to".
日 (sun) — on top; the usual explanation is sun over 正 "straight, correct": what is clear and straight is "right, is". A memory aid, not firm etymology.

example.hanzi: 他就是我一直在等的人。
example.pinyin: Tā jiùshì wǒ yìzhí zài děng de rén.
example.english: He is exactly the person I've been waiting for.
example.fact: 就 on its own already carries an emphatic "precisely this and nothing else", which 就是 sharpens by attaching it to the copula 是 ("to be") — the resulting word is also used constantly as a stand-alone agreement particle in speech ("就是!", "Exactly!/Right!"), functioning almost like an interjection.

examples.english: I just don't want to go.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiùshì wǒ yào de dá'àn.
examples.english: This is exactly the answer I wanted.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — eating and speech: 喝, 吸, 吗; 吃 is to eat.
乞 (qǐ) is only a loose sound clue for chī.

example.pinyin: Nǐ chī fàn le ma?
example.fact: 你吃了吗？ is a traditional everyday greeting, like 'How are you?' 吃 reaches into idioms: 吃醋 'be jealous', 吃惊 'be startled', 吃苦 'endure hardship'. Medicine is 吃药, 'eaten' not 'drunk'.

examples.english: I didn't eat breakfast today.
Let's go have hotpot.

components.note: 斤 (axe) — cutting tools, as in 新 new and 斩 chop. 所 once echoed the sound of chopping; "place" and "that which" are later borrowed uses.
月 (flesh/meat, not moon here) — oldest form is a hand holding a piece of meat, "to possess"; 月 as meat also appears in 肉 words like 肚 belly and 脑 brain.

example.pinyin: Suǒyǒu de xuésheng dōu dào le.
example.fact: 所有 meaning "all" almost always shows up with 都 later in the sentence ("所有...都...") — 所有 modifies the noun, but it's the adverb 都 that actually carries the "without exception" meaning on the verb, and dropping 都 after a 所有-phrase is a common, noticeable slip for English speakers used to "all" doing that job alone.

examples.pinyin: Suǒyǒu de piào dōu mài wán le.
examples.english: All the tickets are sold out.

examples.hanzi: 他花了所有的钱买礼物。
examples.pinyin: Tā huāle suǒyǒu de qián mǎi lǐwù.
examples.english: He spent all his money on gifts.

components.note: 廾 (two hands) — in 開 two hands lift the bar of a gate; 开 is the simplified shape. Compare 关 (close).

example.pinyin: Qǐng kāi mén.
example.fact: 开 is a very flexible verb: 开灯 'turn on the light', 开车 'drive', 开会 'hold a meeting', 开始 'begin', 开玩笑 'joke'. Note that 开 'open' also means 'turn on', not just physical openings.

examples.english: What time does the shop open?
He drives to work every day.

components.note: 一 (one) — a single horizontal stroke is the number one; 二 and 三 just add strokes, so the first three numbers are tally marks.
下 (below) — a mark placed under a line, the mirror of 上 above.

example.pinyin: Děng yíxià, wǒ mǎshàng jiù lái.
example.english: Wait a moment, I'll be right there.
example.fact: 一下 attached after a verb softens and shortens an action into "just a moment of verb-ing" (等一下 "wait a sec", 看一下 "take a quick look") — grammatically it works much like the verb-reduplication pattern behind 谢谢 (also in this batch), just built from a numeral phrase instead of repeating the verb.

examples.pinyin: Ràng wǒ kàn yíxià, hǎo ma?
examples.english: Let me take a look, okay?
He understood right away.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 室 room, 安 safe, 字 character; 家 is home.
豕 (pig) — a pig under a roof: pigs were kept in the home, hence home and family.

example.pinyin: Wǒ jiā yǒu sì kǒu rén.
example.english: There are four people in my family.
example.fact: 家 means 'home' and 'family': 回家 'go home'. It is a suffix for experts (作家 'writer', 科学家 'scientist') and a measure word for businesses (一家店 'a shop'). 大家 means 'everyone'.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā lí xuéxiào hěn jìn.
examples.english: My home is close to school.

examples.pinyin: Tāmen yì jiā rén qù lǚxíng le.
examples.english: The whole family went on a trip.

components.note: 非 (not) — two wings spread in opposite directions, so "opposed, not". Gives sound to 啡 fēi, 排 pái and 悲 bēi.
巾 (cloth) — cloth and clothing, as in 布 cloth, 带 belt, 帽 hat; 常 first meant a long skirt (裳 cháng).
尚 (shàng) is a loose sound clue for cháng; 尚 also sounds out 堂 táng and 掌 zhǎng.

example.pinyin: Zhè dào cài fēicháng hǎochī.
example.fact: 非常 is a stronger, slightly more formal-sounding intensifier than the near-obligatory 很 ("very") that defaults before almost any adjective in a plain statement — reaching for 非常 in every single sentence, where a native speaker would just use 很, is a common tell of a learner overusing the "big" word for "very".

examples.english: It's very cold today.
I miss you a lot.

components.note: 手 (hand) — over 目 (eye): a hand shading the eyes to look into the distance. 目 marks seeing words, as in 眼, 睡.
至 (arrive) — 到 is to arrive.
刂 is the knife form 刀 (dāo), a close sound clue for dào; 到 itself sounds out 倒 dǎo/dào.

example.hanzi: 我在公园里看到了一只小狗。
example.pinyin: Wǒ zài gōngyuán lǐ kàndào le yì zhī xiǎo gǒu.
example.english: I saw a little dog in the park.
example.fact: 看到 pairs the verb 看 ("to look") with the result complement 到 ("to arrive, to achieve") to mark that the looking actually succeeded in perceiving something. The same verb+到 achievement pattern reappears in 找到 (also in this batch, rank 70, "to find") — a productive template for turning a plain effort-verb into a success-verb.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ méi kàndào nǐ de duǎnxìn.
examples.english: I didn't see your text message.

examples.hanzi: 你看到那辆红色的车了吗?
examples.pinyin: Nǐ kàndào nà liàng hóngsè de chē le ma?
examples.english: Did you see that red car?

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — the bottom part, as in 布, 帽, 带. 希 is often read as a loosely woven cloth, so 'sparse, rare'; 希望 hope is a later extension.
乂 (crisscross) — Memory aid: crossed threads in an open weave 乂 on cloth 巾 — thin, rare, something you hope for.
亡 (wáng) is a close sound clue for wàng; it also sounds out 忘 wàng (forget) and 网 wǎng.
月 (moon) — to gaze up at the moon, so to look into the distance, then to hope.

example.hanzi: 我希望明年能去中国旅行。
example.pinyin: Wǒ xīwàng míngnián néng qù Zhōngguó lǚxíng.
example.english: I hope I can travel to China next year.
example.fact: 希望 functions as both a verb ("to hope") and a noun ("a hope, a wish") with no change in form at all — the same free noun/verb flexibility the pilot batch’s 工作 entry (rank 43) describes, so 我的希望 ("my hope") and 我希望 ("I hope") reuse the identical word in two different grammatical roles.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xīwàng nǐ zǎodiǎn hǎo qǐlai.
examples.english: I hope you get better soon.
He is full of hope for the future.

components.note: 阝 on the right is 邑 (city) — places, as in 都 capital, 邮 post, 部 part. 那 was a place name before it meant "that".
此 (cǐ) is a loose sound clue for xiē; 此 also sounds out 紫 zǐ and 雌 cí. 些 is the plural-ish "some, a few".

example.hanzi: 那些照片是我去年拍的。
example.pinyin: Nàxiē zhàopiàn shì wǒ qùnián pāi de.
example.english: Those photos are ones I took last year.
example.fact: 那些 mirrors the pilot batch’s 这些 (rank 37) exactly, just swapping in the far-demonstrative 那 for the near-demonstrative 这 — together with 那样 and 那里 (both also in this batch), it shows the whole 那-family of words tracking one-for-one against its 这-family counterpart.

examples.english: Who are those people?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bù xiǎng chī nàxiē dōngxi.
examples.english: I don't want to eat those things.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — speaking and asking, as in 吗, 呢, 问: 哪 is a question word.
那 (nà) gives the same syllable in a different tone; compare 那 "that" and 哪 "which".

example.pinyin: Nǐ shì nǎ guó rén?
example.fact: 哪 asks 'which' before a measure word: 哪个 'which one', 哪本书. 哪儿 or 哪里 means 'where'. Don't confuse 哪 with 那; the 口 on the left makes it a question. 哪里哪里 is a modest reply to a compliment.

examples.english: Where do you live?
Which one do you like?

components.note: 當 (traditional) — 田 field under 尚 (shàng), 尚 being a loose sound hint for dāng. 当 keeps only a squashed top and a few strokes of it.
尚 (shàng) — the top part of 當; only a loose sound clue today. 当 is dāng (to act as, should) or dàng (appropriate).
灬 (fire) — heat and burning, as in 热 hot, 点 dot, 照 shine. 然 first meant "to burn" (燃 rán adds 火 later); "so, naturally" is borrowed.
肰 (rán) gives the exact sound and shows up in 燃 rán.

example.pinyin: “Nǐ huì lái cānjiā jùhuì ma?” “Dāngrán huì!”
example.english: "Will you come to the party?" "Of course I will!"
example.fact: 当然 sits toward the confident end of Mandarin’s certainty spectrum — stronger than 也许 (also in this batch, "perhaps") and close in strength to 肯定 (also in this batch) — but 当然 specifically frames something as obvious or expected, rather than merely asserting that it’s true.

examples.english: Of course you can, please come in.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ dāngrán bú yòng fù qián.
examples.english: Of course you don't have to pay.

components.note: 也 (also) — began as a picture (a vessel or snake; scholars disagree) and was borrowed for 'also'. A loose sound clue in 他 tā, 她 tā, 地 dì, 池 chí.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢: giving permission is spoken.
午 (wǔ) is only a loose sound clue for xǔ.

example.pinyin: Tā yěxǔ yǐjīng dào jiā le.
example.fact: 也许 is a near-synonym of 可能 ("maybe, possible") — 也许 leans a shade more literary and typically opens a clause as a sentence adverb, while 可能 moves more freely and can also stand in as a noun meaning "possibility," as the pilot batch’s own 可能 entry (rank 27) already notes.

examples.pinyin: Tā jīntiān yěxǔ bú huì lái.
examples.english: He may not come today.
Maybe it'll rain tomorrow.

components.note: 彳 (step) — left half of a crossroads: 行 pictures a crossroads, so to go, and (háng) a row or trade.

example.pinyin: Zhèyàng xíng ma?
example.fact: 行 is a common 'OK': 行！ 'Sure!', 不行 'won't do'. As háng it means 'row' or 'profession' (银行 'bank', 内行 'expert'). 旅行 'travel' keeps the walking sense.

examples.english: Coming tomorrow is fine too.

examples.pinyin: Bù xíng, zhèlǐ bù néng tíngchē.
examples.english: No, you can't park here.

components.note: 朋 (friend) — oldest form shows two strings of cowrie shells (old money) side by side; they paired up and came to mean companions.
又 (hand) — two hands 又 stacked: hands joined in friendship.

example.pinyin: Tā shì wǒ zuì hǎo de péngyou.
example.fact: 朋 alone is already a pictograph of two people (or two strings of shells) side by side, and 友 separately pictures two hands clasped together — 朋友 doubles up two independently "companionship"-themed pictographs into one word, the same word-building strategy the pilot batch’s 喜欢 and 应该 entries use for fusing near-synonymous halves.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de péngyou zài Běijīng gōngzuò.
examples.english: My friend works in Beijing.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ yǒu hěn duō Zhōngguó péngyou ma?
examples.english: Do you have many Chinese friends?

components.note: 女 (woman) — women and family, as in 她, 姐, 奶; 妈 is mother.
马 (mǎ) is a close sound clue for mā; also in 吗 ma, 骂 mà and 码 mǎ.
女 (woman) — women and family, as in 她, 姐, 奶; 妈 is mother.
马 (mǎ) is a close sound clue for mā; also in 吗 ma, 骂 mà and 码 mǎ.

example.hanzi: 妈妈每天早上都做早饭。
example.pinyin: Māma měitiān zǎoshang dōu zuò zǎofàn.
example.fact: 妈妈 is 妈 reduplicated with a toneless second syllable — the same doubling pattern behind 爸爸 (also in this batch) — and this kind of babyish reduplication for "mom/dad" recurs across unrelated language families (mama, papa), likely because doubled syllables are among the easiest sounds for infants to produce.

examples.english: Mom, I'm hungry.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ māma shì yì míng yīshēng.
examples.english: My mother is a doctor.

components.note: 目 (eye) — looking; an eye turned on a tree 木, hence to look at, and mutually looking: "each other". 相 also gives 想 xiǎng, 箱 xiāng and 湘 xiāng.
亻 (person) — a person and his word: 言 (speech) beside it gives a person who keeps his word, hence "trust, believe".
言 (speech) — written 讠 on the left of other characters, as in 说, 请, 谢.

example.pinyin: Wǒ xiāngxìn tā shuō de shì zhēn de.
example.english: I believe what he said is true.
example.fact: 相信 expresses trust or conviction that something is reliable or true, distinct from 认为 and 以为 (both also in this batch), which introduce a personal opinion or judgment rather than an act of trust — 相信他 ("to trust him") and 认为他对 ("to think he’s right") reach for different verbs even though English "believe" can cover both.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bù xiāngxìn tā de huà.
examples.english: I don't believe what he says.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng xiāngxìn wǒ, wǒ bú huì piàn nǐ.
examples.english: Please believe me, I won't lie to you.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — the right-hand side. Usually about cutting (到, 别, 利), but not in 前: it is a later corruption of the old picture.
舟 (boat) — hidden in the old form: a foot on a boat moving ahead, so 'in front, forward'. Usual explanation, though the modern shape hides it.

example.pinyin: Tā zhàn zài wǒ qiánmiàn.
example.english: He is standing in front of me.
example.fact: 前 works for both space and time: 前面 'in front', 以前 'before', 前天 'the day before yesterday', 前年 'the year before last'. For 'former' it is a prefix: 前男友 'ex-boyfriend'.

examples.english: Please wash your hands before eating.
The bank is just ahead.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — marks speech, sounds and eating, as in 叫 call, 吃 eat, 唱 sing; 嗨 is hi or hey, a greeting.
海 (hǎi) — close sound: 嗨 hāi; same part as in 海 sea.

example.pinyin: Hāi, hǎojiǔ bú jiàn!
example.fact: 嗨 is a borrowing of English 'hi', widely used in informal greetings. It is also an older exclamation of regret or realization: 嗨，别提了！ 'Ugh, don't even mention it!' For proper greetings, 你好 is more standard.

examples.english: Hi, how are you today?
Hey, I'm over here!

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; recognising something is naming it.
人 (rén) gives the exact sound, and also means "person".
力 (strength) — visible inside 为. Memory aid: putting strength 力 into doing something; 为 is 'to do, to act' and, in 因为, 为什么, 'because/for'.
為 (traditional) — often explained as a hand leading an elephant to work. 为 is a cursive simplification, so the picture is no longer visible.

example.hanzi: 大部分人都认为这是个好主意。
example.pinyin: Dàbùfen rén dōu rènwéi zhè shì gè hǎo zhǔyi.
example.english: Most people think this is a good idea.
example.fact: 认为 sits at the more formal, reasoned end of Mandarin’s "think" verbs — the pilot batch’s 觉得 entry (rank 23) already contrasts with it as the more common, subjective-feeling "think," while 认为 shows up disproportionately in writing, argument, and reporting rather than casual chat.

examples.hanzi: 你认为这个办法怎么样?
examples.english: What do you think of this method?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ rènwéi tā shuō de duì.
examples.english: I think he's right.

components.note: 丬 (bed/couch, left side) — the left strip, a bed seen sideways. Dictionary story: going to bed at night, the 'future' that is sure to come; read as a memory aid.
夕 (evening) — upper part of the right side, as in 外 and 多; with 寸 (hand/inch) it frames 将 meaning 'about to / will'.

example.pinyin: Gōngsī jiāng zài míngnián kāiyè.
example.english: The company will open next year.
example.fact: 将 is a formal 'will/about to', common in news and announcements; speech prefers 要 or 会. 将来 means 'the future'. As jiàng it means 'general': 将军, 大将.

examples.hanzi: 飞机将在十分钟后起飞。
examples.pinyin: Fēijī jiāng zài shí fēnzhōng hòu qǐfēi.
examples.english: The plane will take off in ten minutes.

examples.hanzi: 新的地铁站将于明年开放。
examples.pinyin: Xīn de dìtiězhàn jiāng yú míngnián kāifàng.
examples.english: The new subway station will open next year.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement and place, as in 道 way, 过 pass, 近 near; the radical hints at "here / this way". The 文 part is not a useful sound clue.
儿 (child, legs) — shows a person's legs; in 兒 the top was a child's soft skull. As an ending (这儿) it adds the er sound; 儿 also in 先, 兄, 光.

example.pinyin: Nǐ qù nàr, wǒ qù zhèr.
example.english: You go there, I'll go here.
example.fact: 这儿 attaches the colloquial "erhua" (儿化) suffix -r directly onto 这 — the same Beijing-flavored rhotacization the pilot batch’s 这里 entry (rank 17) already flags as a regional variant. 这儿/那儿 are the casual, spoken-register counterparts to 这里/那里 (also in this batch).

examples.pinyin: Nǐ zài zhèr děng wǒ yíxià.
examples.english: Wait for me here for a moment.
The food here is delicious.

components.note: 今 (now, today) — gives sound to 琴 qín, 含 hán, 念 niàn and 吟 yín; the old picture is uncertain.
大 (big person) — a person with a line above the head, marking the sky above; tiān = heaven, sky, day.

example.pinyin: Jīntiān tiānqì hěn hǎo.
example.fact: 今 alone already carries the sense "now, the present" (the same root behind 现在 in the pilot batch, rank 10, and 如今), while 天 supplies "day" — 今天 combines them transparently into "the present day," the same logic behind 明天 ("tomorrow") and 昨天 ("yesterday").

examples.english: Today is my birthday.
Are you busy today?

components.note: 日 (sun) — the sun beside the moon: two light sources, so bright and clear.
月 (moon) — as in 朋, 期, 有; here it brightens the night.
白 (white, bright) — gives sound to 拍 pāi, 怕 pà, 伯 bó and 泊 bó. Meaning: white, clear, plain, hence "明白" understand.

example.hanzi: 老师讲了两次,我才明白。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī jiǎng le liǎng cì, wǒ cái míngbai.
example.english: The teacher explained it twice before I understood.
example.fact: 明白 marks a flash of comprehension — grasping how or why something works — while 知道 (pilot batch, rank 3) simply marks awareness that a fact exists. A speaker can 知道 a rule exists without yet being able to say they 明白 it, a distinction English’s single verb "to know/understand" doesn’t force you to make.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bù míngbai nǐ de yìsi.
examples.english: I don't understand what you mean.
What he said is very clear.

components.note: 一 (one) — a single horizontal stroke is the number one; 二 and 三 just add strokes, so the first three numbers are tally marks.
目 (eye) — sighting along a straight line. 直 also sounds out 值 zhí and 植 zhí.

example.pinyin: Tā yìzhí zài děng nǐ de diànhuà.
example.english: She has been waiting for your call the whole time.
example.fact: 一直 combines "one" with 直 ("straight") into an image of an unbroken straight line — the same 一 + [verb/adjective] pattern behind the pilot batch’s 一起 (一 + 起, "rise," rank 40) and this batch’s own 一切 and 一定. Extended metaphorically, it means an action or state continuing straight through without interruption, whether in time (一直等, "waiting the whole time") or space (一直走, "go straight ahead").

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yìzhí zhù zài zhège chéngshì.
examples.english: I've always lived in this city.

examples.hanzi: 一直往前走,就到银行了。
examples.pinyin: Yìzhí wǎng qián zǒu, jiù dào yínháng le.
examples.english: Go straight ahead and you'll reach the bank.

components.note: 手 (hand) — over 目 (eye): a hand shading the eyes to look into the distance. 目 marks seeing words, as in 眼, 睡.
手 (hand) — over 目 (eye): a hand shading the eyes to look into the distance. 目 marks seeing words, as in 眼, 睡.

example.pinyin: Ràng wǒ kànkan zhè běn shū.
example.english: Let me take a look at this book.
example.fact: 看看 reduplicates the verb 看 with a neutral-tone second syllable — exactly the "soften a request" pattern the pilot batch’s 谢谢 entry (rank 21) already names 看看 as an example of. Repeating a one-syllable verb makes the action sound brief and casual, much like English "just take a quick look."

examples.english: How about taking a look at this?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ qù kànkan tā zài bu zài jiā.
examples.english: I'll go see whether he's home.

components.note: 车 (cart) — simplified from 車, a wheeled cart seen from above. As a radical it marks vehicles: 转 turn, 轮 wheel, 较.

example.pinyin: Wǒ zuò chē qù shàngbān.
example.english: I take the car to work.
example.fact: 车 is a general word for any wheeled vehicle: 汽车 'car', 火车 'train', 自行车 'bicycle', 出租车 'taxi'. Its measure word is 辆. In Chinese chess the piece 车 is the 'chariot' (rook).

examples.pinyin: Zhè liàng qìchē shì xīn mǎi de.
examples.english: This car was newly bought.
Do you have a bicycle?

components.note: 日 (sun) — day and time, as in 晴 clear, 早 early, 明 bright; time was read from the sun.
寸 (cùn) stands in for 寺 sì in the traditional 時; sound clue is loose. 寺 also gives 诗 shī and 持 chí.

example.pinyin: Nǐ shénme shíhou lái?
example.fact: 时候 means 'the time when': …的时候 'when…'. 小时 is 'hour', 时间 'time', and 有时 'sometimes'. The simplified form 时 reshapes the old 時.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎo shíhou zhù zài xiāngxia.
examples.english: I lived in the countryside as a child.

examples.hanzi: 有时候我坐公交车上班。
examples.pinyin: Yǒu shíhou wǒ zuò gōngjiāochē shàngbān.
examples.english: Sometimes I take the bus to work.

components.note: 乂 (to cut, crisscross) — old for mowing or cutting. Dictionary story: someone cut down 乂 and buried in a wooden coffin 木, a vivid memory aid.
木 (tree, wood) — the bottom. In 杀 it is a leftover of the old 殺 form rather than meaning wood; 殺 also had 殳 (weapon in hand).

example.pinyin: Nóngmín shā le yì zhī jī.
example.fact: 杀 is used literally for killing and also figuratively: 杀价 'bargain hard', 杀毒 'run antivirus', 杀菌 'sterilize'.

examples.english: Grandma is cleaning a fish in the kitchen.

examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng yào kěyǐ shā chóng.
examples.english: This medicine can kill insects.

components.note: 土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 场 field, 城 city, 坐 sit.
也 (yě) is a loose sound clue for dì; 也 also sounds out 他 tā and 池 chí.
方 (square, direction) — early picture is disputed (a plough-like tool or lashed boats). Sound clue in 房 fáng, 防 fáng, 访 fǎng, 放 fàng.
亠 (lid) — the top. Memory aid: a lid over a bent shape — a square-cornered 'side' or place, as in 地方, 方法.

example.pinyin: Zhè shì yí gè ānjìng de dìfang.
example.fact: The pinyin here reflects the neutral-toned reading dìfang, the everyday word for "place, location" that actually explains this word’s top-100 frequency rank. Dictionaries also record a separate, fully-toned reading dìfāng, reserved for the narrower administrative sense "local, regional" (as opposed to 中央, "central") — the same one-hanzi-string, two-register-readings split as 告诉 in the earlier batch.

examples.english: Where do you live?
I've been to this place before.

meanings: anyway (to get back to a previous topic)

components.note: 一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
辶 (walk) — movement, as in 这, 近, 送: 过 is to pass or cross.
寸 here replaces 咼 (guō) of the traditional 過, so it is not a sound clue; 咼 survives in 锅 guō and 祸 huò.

example.hanzi: 这个包很贵,不过质量真的很好。
example.pinyin: Zhège bāo hěn guì, búguò zhìliàng zhēn de hěn hǎo.
example.english: This bag is expensive, but the quality is really good.
example.fact: 不过 is the softest, most casual member of Mandarin’s "but" trio, as the pilot batch’s 但是 entry (rank 18) already lays out: 但是 is neutral and standard, 可是 a shade more conversational, and 不过 the softest of the three — useful for gauging register when contrasting two ideas.

examples.english: I was only joking.

examples.hanzi: 他不过十岁,已经会做饭了。
examples.pinyin: Tā búguò shí suì, yǐjīng huì zuòfàn le.
examples.english: He's only ten, and he already knows how to cook.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — marks speech, sounds and eating, as in 叫 call, 吃 eat, 唱 sing; 呃 is a hesitation sound, uh, or a hiccup.
厄 (è) — same sound: 呃 è. 厄 also sounds out 扼 è.

example.pinyin: È, wǒ bú tài quèdìng.
example.fact: 呃 is a filler sound that shows hesitation, like 'er' or 'um'. It can also imitate a hiccup. It appears mostly in dialogue and chat messages, and is rare in formal writing.

examples.pinyin: È, ràng wǒ zài kǎolǜ yíxià.
examples.english: Er, let me think about it again.
Er, what did you say again?

components.note: 发 (send out, hair) — two characters merged in simplified writing: 發 fā "emit, issue" and 髮 fà "hair" (头发).
土 (earth) — a green shoot pushing up from the ground: growth, birth, life. 生 also sounds out 性 xìng, 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.

example.hanzi: 昨天晚上发生了一件奇怪的事。
example.pinyin: Zuótiān wǎnshang fāshēng le yí jiàn qíguài de shì.
example.english: A strange thing happened last night.
example.fact: 发生 is reserved for events, incidents, and changes of state — never for a person or object’s own physical arrival, which instead uses verbs like 到 or 来. Its second character 生 (also picturing new growth breaking out of the earth, as seen in the pilot batch’s 先生 entry, rank 25) frames an event as "growing into" existence.

examples.english: What happened here?

examples.hanzi: 我不想让这种事再发生。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bù xiǎng ràng zhè zhǒng shì zài fāshēng.
examples.english: I don't want this to happen again.

components.note: 几 (small table) — a low table with legs. As a sound it gives jī to 机 and 肌, and means how many in 几个.

example.pinyin: Nǐ yǒu jǐ ge háizi?
example.english: How many children do you have?
example.fact: 几 asks about small numbers (typically under ten): 几点 'what time', 几岁 'how old (a child)'. For large or unknown amounts use 多少. It also means 'several': 几天 'a few days'. Read jī, it means 'small table', as in 茶几.

examples.english: What's the date today?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ děngle nǐ hǎo jǐ ge xiǎoshí.
examples.english: I waited for you for several hours.

components.note: 回 (return) — a swirl or whirlpool drawn as nested squares: it turns around and comes back.
来 (come) — it began as a picture of a wheat plant; the sound was borrowed for "come". 麦 (wheat) still shows it, with a root 夂 added.

example.pinyin: Nǐ shénme shíhou huílai?
example.fact: 回来 anchors the "return" action toward the speaker’s own location — swap 来 ("toward here") for 去 ("toward there") and 回去 means "to go back" to somewhere else instead. The same toward-speaker/away-from-speaker contrast also distinguishes 出来 and 过来 (both also in this batch) from their 去-counterparts.

examples.english: He'll be back tomorrow.

examples.hanzi: 你回来的时候给我打电话。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ huílái de shíhou gěi wǒ dǎ diànhuà.
examples.english: Call me when you get back.

components.note: 冫 (ice) — cold, as in 冷 cold, 冰 ice, 冻 freeze; here it stands for 氵 water in 準 (a water level, so exact).
隹 (zhuī, short-tailed bird) gives only a loose sound clue for zhǔn.
田 (field) — the bottom part. 备 is simplified from 備; the dictionary story is a trip to the 田 field to prepare for harvest. Treat it as a memory aid.
夂 (going down, slow step) — the top. Memory aid: heading 夂 to the field 田 to get ready — 准备, 设备.

example.pinyin: Wǒmen zhèngzài zhǔnbèi wǎnfàn.
example.english: We are preparing dinner right now.
example.fact: 准备 doubles as an auxiliary verb meaning "to be about to, to intend to" right before another verb (准备走了, "about to leave"), on top of its plainer sense "to prepare, get ready" — one of several Chinese verbs, alongside 要 and 打算, that slide from a full action verb into signaling near-future intention.

examples.english: Are you ready?

examples.pinyin: Tā zài zhǔnbèi míngtiān de kǎoshì.
examples.english: He's preparing for tomorrow's exam.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打 hit, 拿 take, 把 hold; 找 is to search with the hands. The right part 戈 is not a useful clue.
至 (arrive) — 到 is to arrive.
刂 is the knife form 刀 (dāo), a close sound clue for dào; 到 itself sounds out 倒 dǎo/dào.

example.hanzi: 我终于找到了我的钥匙。
example.pinyin: Wǒ zhōngyú zhǎodào le wǒ de yàoshi.
example.fact: 找到 is built from the same verb+到 achievement pattern as 看到 (also in this batch, rank 51) — 找 alone only names the act of searching, and adding 到 confirms the search actually succeeded. Without it, 我找钥匙 just means "I’m looking for my keys," with no guarantee they turned up.

examples.english: Have you found a job?

examples.hanzi: 我在桌子下面找到了手机。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài zhuōzi xiàmian zhǎodào le shǒujī.
examples.english: I found my phone under the table.

components.note: 后 (after, behind) — two words merged in simplified writing: old 后 "ruler" (皇后 empress) and 後 "behind, later" (as in 然后).

example.pinyin: Chī fàn hòu wǒ qù sànbù.
example.english: I go for a walk after eating.
example.fact: In simplified Chinese 后 took over for the traditional 後 'after, behind', and the older 后 'queen' (皇后) merged with it. 以后 means 'afterwards', 后面 'behind', 后天 'the day after tomorrow'.

examples.english: After class we'll go eat.

examples.pinyin: Xuéxiào hòumiàn yǒu yí ge gōngyuán.
examples.english: There is a park behind the school.

components.note: 父 (father) — a father-word radical, as in 爷 grandpa; 爸 is dad.
巴 (bā) is a close sound clue for bà; 巴 also sounds out 吧 ba, 把 bǎ and 爸 bà.
父 (father) — a father-word radical, as in 爷 grandpa; 爸 is dad.
巴 (bā) is a close sound clue for bà; 巴 also sounds out 吧 ba, 把 bǎ and 爸 bà.

example.pinyin: Bàba zài kàn diànshì.
example.fact: 爸 shares a root with the more formal, literary word for "father," 父, while the doubled, neutral-toned 爸爸 is the affectionate, everyday form children actually use — roughly parallel to how English distinguishes the formal "father" from the everyday "dad/daddy."

examples.english: Dad is working overtime today.
My dad likes fishing.

components.note: 一 (one) — a single horizontal stroke is the number one; 二 and 三 just add strokes, so the first three numbers are tally marks.
刀 (knife, written 刂 on the right) — cutting, as in 分 divide, 刻 carve, 到 arrive.
七 (qī) is a close sound clue for qiē/qiè.

example.pinyin: Yíqiè dōu huì hǎo qǐlai de.
example.fact: 一切 combines "one" with 切 (built from 刀 "knife" + 七, its phonetic — literally "to cut") into an old image of "everything cut into one whole." Like the pilot batch’s 所有 entry (rank 48), it typically appears with 都 later in the sentence to land the "without exception" meaning on the verb, rather than carrying that force alone.

examples.english: He wants to know all of this.
Everything is ready.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打 hit, 拿 take, 把 hold; 抱 is to hug or hold in the arms.
包 (bāo) is a close sound clue for bào; it also sounds out 跑 pǎo, 饱 bǎo and 炮 pào.
欠 (lack, yawn) — open mouth or something missing, as in 次 and 欢; 歉 is feeling short, hence sorry.
兼 (jiān) is a loose sound clue for qiàn; 兼 also sounds out 嫌 xián and 谦 qiān.

example.pinyin: Bàoqiàn, wǒ lái wǎn le.
example.fact: 抱歉 sits a notch more formal than the everyday 对不起 (also in this batch) — common in announcements, customer service, and written apologies ("抱歉给您带来不便," "sorry for the inconvenience"), whereas 对不起 is the default spoken apology between friends and strangers alike.

examples.pinyin: Bàoqiàn, ràng nǐ jiǔ děng le.
examples.english: Sorry to have kept you waiting.
I'm sorry to bother you.

components.note: 比 (compare) — two people side by side, one lined up with the other; to compare.

example.pinyin: Tā bǐ wǒ gāo.
example.fact: The comparison pattern is A 比 B + adjective: 他比我高. Don't add 很 or 非常 after 比; use 更, 还 or an amount: 高三厘米 'three cm taller'. 比 also means 'compete' in 比赛 'match' and 'ratio' in 比例.

examples.pinyin: Jīntiān bǐ zuótiān lěng duō le.
examples.english: Today is much colder than yesterday.

examples.pinyin: Tā pǎobù bǐ wǒ kuài duō le.
examples.english: He runs much faster than I do.

components.note: 心 (heart) — feelings and thoughts, as in 想, 思, 急; 感 is to feel or be moved.
咸 (xián) is a loose sound clue for gǎn; 咸 also sounds out 喊 hǎn and 减 jiǎn.
见 (see) — seeing and perceiving, as in 现, 看, 视: 觉 is to sense and become aware (jué), also "sleep" (jiào) in 睡觉.
The top is a shape of 学 (xué), a loose sound hint from the traditional 覺.

example.pinyin: Wǒ gǎnjué jīntiān tèbié lèi.
example.fact: 感觉 shares its second character with the pilot batch’s 觉得 (rank 23) — both use 觉, "to perceive" — but 感觉 leans toward physical sensations and gut impressions (累, 冷, 不舒服), while 觉得 more often introduces an opinion or judgment about something external, a subtle overlap that trips up learners reaching for "feel" in English.

examples.english: How are you feeling?

examples.hanzi: 这个房间给我一种温暖的感觉。
examples.pinyin: Zhège fángjiān gěi wǒ yì zhǒng wēnnuǎn de gǎnjué.
examples.english: This room gives me a warm feeling.

components.note: 此 (cǐ) is a loose sound clue for xiē; 此 also sounds out 紫 zǐ and 雌 cí. 些 is the plural-ish "some, a few".

example.pinyin: Wǒ mǎi le yìxiē shuǐguǒ.
example.fact: 些 almost never stands alone: 一些 'some', 这些 'these', 那些 'those', 有些 'some of'. It works for countable and uncountable nouns: 一些水 'some water'. For a smaller amount, 一点儿 is common.

examples.english: Whose things are these?
Please give me some water.

components.note: 只 (only; measure word) — two old characters merged: 隻 zhī "a single (bird), measure word" and 只 zhǐ "only".
日 (sun) — on top; the usual explanation is sun over 正 "straight, correct": what is clear and straight is "right, is". A memory aid, not firm etymology.

example.pinyin: Wǒ zhǐshì xiǎng bāng nǐ yí gè máng.
example.english: I just wanted to help you out.
example.fact: 只是 often works less as a plain "merely" and more as a softening hedge right before explaining a real reason, especially at the start of a mild objection or excuse ("我只是...", "It’s just that I...") — much like English speakers reach for "I just..." to make a statement sound less confrontational.

examples.english: He's just a child.

examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǐshì yí ge xiǎo wèntí.
examples.english: This is only a small problem.

components.note: 心 (heart) — feelings and thought, as in 想 think, 思 ponder, 急 anxious; in 怎 it is only loosely linked to the question sense.
乍 (zhà) is a loose sound clue for zěn; 乍 also sounds out 作 zuò, 昨 zuó and 炸 zhà.
幺 (tiny, a thread) — 么 looks like 幺 and was borrowed as a simplified form for the light particle in 什么, 怎么, 这么. The shape does not explain the meaning today.
厶 (loop) — the visible lower part, a small curl. Memory aid: a tiny stroke 丿 over a curl — a 'little something' you ask about: 什么 what?
木 (tree) — wood, as in 桌 table, 板 board; 样 once meant a tree (acorn) and later "form, pattern".
羊 (yáng, sheep) is a near-exact sound clue for yàng; 羊 also sounds out 洋 yáng and 养 yǎng.

example.hanzi: 这个周末去爬山,怎么样?
example.pinyin: Zhège zhōumò qù páshān, zěnmeyàng?
example.english: How about going hiking this weekend?
example.fact: 怎么样 extends the pilot batch’s 怎么 (rank 9) with the added suffix 样 ("appearance, kind"), and the pilot’s own 怎么 entry already flags the payoff: 怎么样 stands alone as a complete question about quality or status ("How is it?"), while bare 怎么 needs a following verb to ask "how" an action is done.

examples.english: How was your day today?
How about this piece of clothing?

components.note: 凵 (open pit) — oldest form shows a foot stepping out of a pit or cave: to go out, come out.
来 (come) — it began as a picture of a wheat plant; the sound was borrowed for "come". 麦 (wheat) still shows it, with a root 夂 added.

example.pinyin: Tàiyáng chūlái le.
example.fact: Beyond its literal sense, 出来 works as a productive verb-complement suffix meaning "to emerge into being" (想出来, "to think up [an idea]") or "to manage to tell by looking" (看出来) — the same kind of layered, abstract extension piling onto a literal directional verb that the pilot batch’s 起来 entry (rank 35) describes.

examples.pinyin: Tā cóng fángjiān lǐ chūlái le.
examples.english: He came out of the room.

examples.hanzi: 我听出来了,这是你的声音。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ tīng chūlái le, zhè shì nǐ de shēngyīn.
examples.english: I can tell it's you by your voice.

components.note: 一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
要 (want, need) — oldest form shows hands at a waist: it meant "waist" (腰 yāo adds 月 flesh); "essential" followed.

example.pinyin: Búyào chídào le!
example.fact: 不要 is Mandarin’s standard prohibitive — negating the modal 要 ("must, will") with 不 to forbid an action — and it’s commonly clipped to just 别 in casual speech (别迟到, same meaning) — two completely different-looking words doing the identical job of "don’t."

examples.english: Don't worry.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bú yào zhège, wǒ yào nàge.
examples.english: I don't want this one, I want that one.

components.note: 寸 (hand, inch) — hands and measuring, as in 寻 seek, 导 lead, 射 shoot; 对 faces someone or matches a pair. 又 here only stands in for the left side of 對.
一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
走 (walk, run) — movement, as in 赶 chase, 超 surpass, 越 cross over; 起 is to rise or get up.
己 (jǐ) is a loose sound clue for qǐ; 己 also sounds out 记 jì and 纪 jì.

example.pinyin: Duìbuqǐ, wǒ bú shì gùyì de.
example.fact: 对不起’s pieces are often parsed as 对 ("to face") plus 不起 ("unable to manage," the same negative-potential pattern behind 买不起, "can’t afford," and 看不起, "to look down on") — a vivid folk-style breakdown of being too ashamed to face someone, now worn down into Mandarin’s default spoken "I’m sorry."

examples.english: Sorry, I don't know.
He said sorry.

components.note: 门 (mén, gate) is a close sound clue for wèn; the picture is asking at a gate, as in 闻 wén.
口 (mouth) — speaking, as in 吃, 唱, 叫: asking is a mouth action.

example.hanzi: 我可以问你一个问题吗？
example.pinyin: Wǒ kěyǐ wèn nǐ yí ge wèntí ma?
example.english: May I ask you a question?
example.fact: 问 takes the person asked directly: 问老师 'ask the teacher'. 请问 starts a polite question, 问好 means 'say hello (on behalf of)'. 问题 means both 'question' and 'problem'.

examples.english: I'd like to ask for directions.
If you don't understand, ask the teacher.
